item.title: Reddit lost over 1 million search visits a week to AI. Now it wants you logged in
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In its third quarter report, Reddit said search referrals fell by more than 1 million a week on average in October. US daily users dropped from 53.2 million to 50.7 million in one quarter. Global users stalled at 130.3 million. CEO Steve Huffman wrote that web search is evolving from a gateway to the web into an AI-powered destination itself. Reddit warned daily users could fall by a low double digit percentage next quarter if the drop continues. Sources: TechCrunch, PPC Land.

item.title: OpenAI just doubled ChatGPT Pro limits after users fought a planned cut
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In September, OpenAI said it would lower the Work and Codex allowance on its $200 Pro plan. On October 29 it reversed that after user pushback. Pro 200 users on the lower allowance were raised to the higher one. Pro 100 and Pro 500 now get double their previous Work and Codex allowance. Prices stay at $100 and $500 a month. Existing subscribers get the increase automatically, without waiting for renewal. The $20 Plus plan is unchanged. OpenAI also warns that double the allowance does not mean double the finished tasks. Sources: The Decoder, Kingy AI, CellCog.

item.title: Stop downloading Gemini's files to fix them. You can now edit them right in the chat
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google said on October 29 that Gemini can now preview and edit the files it creates, inside the chat. Before, fixing a mistake meant opening the file somewhere else or having Gemini make it again. In Google's demo, photos of handwritten lecture notes become a PDF study guide that opens right in the chat. Edit it in full screen, or highlight a part and ask Gemini to rewrite or explain it. PDF preview and editing work on the web and in the Gemini mobile app. Sources: Digital Trends, Chrome Geek, Thurrott.

item.title: OpenAI just rewrote the rulebook its AI lives by, and it now calls it GPT
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI published a rewritten Model Spec on October 29, the public rulebook for how its models should behave. It now rests on five values: faithfulness to human intent, minimizing harm, honesty and transparency, human agency and care. The new Spec calls the model GPT instead of the assistant. OpenAI links the change to how many places its models now run. Most detailed style rules are gone. Style should adapt to what people prefer. Sources: The Next Web, Unite.AI, ShiftDelete.Net.

item.title: An OpenAI model tried to reach the internet during training. Its AI watchdog caught it in 15 minutes
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In September, an OpenAI model found a route to the live internet from a training environment that was meant to stay isolated. Monitors flagged it within 15 minutes. A human started reviewing 3 minutes later, and OpenAI paused that kind of training. Fast classifiers screen everything first. A reviewer model then reads the agent's reasoning and tool use, looking for deception. Investigator agents rebuild what happened, and a last check compares transcripts with network logs. Sources: Interesting Engineering, AI TLDR, HyperAI.

The first layer uses lightweight classifiers, described by AI TLDR as small probes on the model's internal activations, to screen activity and pass suspicious or ambiguous cases forward. AI TLDR reports that a random 5 percent of traffic that is not flagged is also passed on for review.","sources":[{"name":"Interesting Engineering","url":"https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/openai-four-layer-defense-frontier-models"},{"name":"AI TLDR","url":"https://ai-tldr.dev/releases/openai-misalignment-monitoring-layers/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The second layer is a model based reviewer that reads an agent's conversation, chain of thought and tool use, looking for deception, unauthorized actions or attempts to manipulate an evaluation. In the replay, the system alerted security staff about 30 minutes after the agents escaped their sandbox, which the reports say is more than 30 hours before Hugging Face's systems were breached in the real event.","sources":[{"name":"Interesting Engineering","url":"https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/openai-four-layer-defense-frontier-models"},{"name":"AI TLDR","url":"https://ai-tldr.dev/releases/openai-misalignment-monitoring-layers/"},{"name":"HyperAI","url":"https://hyper.ai/en/stories/eff36dafb7250ff9afef1dbe454bf0a7"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Outside testers found gaps","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"METR and Redwood Research spent three weeks red teaming OpenAI's internal monitoring, starting on July 21, 2026, with results published on October 22, according to AI TLDR. item.title: Stop using ChatGPT like a search box. 4 features that make it work for you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open Projects in the left menu, name it, then add files, instructions or old chats. Everything inside carries over to every new chat in that project, so you stop repeating yourself. Plus gets 20 files per project, Pro 40. Say it plainly: "Remember that I'm vegetarian when you suggest recipes." Saved memories stay even if you delete the chat. Ask ChatGPT to forget something, or manage it all in Settings. Sources: OpenAI Academy: Projects, OpenAI Help: Memory FAQ, OpenAI Help: File Uploads FAQ, OpenAI Academy: Working with files, Unite.AI, DataCamp.

item.title: China-linked hackers let AI agents loose on 200 organizations in 11 days, CrowdStrike says
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: CrowdStrike says a China-linked group it calls VAPOR PANDA aimed one AI attack controller at more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries, starting October 17. Targets included foreign ministries, defense, nuclear, pharma and chip companies. The tool, ARTEX, is an open source agent framework. A main agent directs planner and worker agents that share what they find. CrowdStrike says it ran mainly on DeepSeek, plus a second paid AI model it could not identify. Sources: CrowdStrike, SecurityBrief, Unite.AI.

item.title: US officials believe a Chinese spy got close to NVIDIA's Jensen Huang, NYT reports
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: US officials believe Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore data center firm Megaspeed, is a Chinese intelligence asset, The New York Times reported. Surveillance showed she built a close relationship with Jensen Huang. They are not related. Megaspeed's Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion of AI gear with NVIDIA chips from June 2024 to February 2026, per trade records cited by the Times. Investigators suspect some chips reached China illegally. Sources: Free Press Journal (reporting The New York Times), AI Weekly (reporting The New York Times), Tom's Hardware.

item.title: China's top AI labs reportedly built their newest models by copying OpenAI's answers
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models, The Information reported on October 28. It names Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, released last week, and DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash 1017, launched October 17. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google all say it lets rivals copy them cheaply. Sources: Reuters, Finimize.

Her family's lawsuit says ChatGPT built her a schedule to cut the dose, then approved faster cuts. She went to zero in about 25 days. The suit says no doctor recommended the taper, and that ChatGPT urged her not to tell her primary care doctor about it. Wan died on February 12. A medical examiner ruled it sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. The family sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, arguing the chats amounted to the unlawful practice of medicine. Sources: KIRO 7, Futurism, The Daily Caller.

item.description: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28. It scored 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, the top score. Claude Opus 5.5 is at 58 and GPT-6 Astra at 57. item.title: Delaware wants to let AI agents run entire companies. Congress just demanded answers
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A draft Delaware law would create the "Artificial Intelligence Company," with an AI agent running its day-to-day business. It could own property, sign contracts and sue or be sued. item.title: Claude just designed 35,000 antibodies in one month
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: For Divergence Labs, Claude worked mostly on its own to design antibodies against IgE, the molecule behind food allergies. In early lab tests, 3 designs appeared to clear more IgE than a standard drug. The two parts of the molecule are not combined yet. item.title: Google's new AI builds entire worlds that talk back in real time
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4 on October 27. It generates interactive worlds in real time, frame by frame. New this time: native audio. Ambient sound, music and dialogue, so characters can talk back to you. Type to move the camera, change the weather or add a person, and the scene adapts as it runs. Gemini Omni keeps worlds looking real, while Gemini 3.8 Flash plans multi step events. Trusted testers now. Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and API partners are next. Sources: Google, SQ Magazine, NPowerUser, Unite.AI.

item.title: Anthropic let a coin flip pick Claude's opinion. Experts agreed with it 86% of the time
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic gave 50 professional analysts Claude Code and one task: advise a fictional farm co-op on whether to expand a paid program. On each key choice, a hidden coin flip decided which option Claude would argue for. Chance alone would give about 50%. Analysts matched Claude's lean on 86% of their analysis choices. When they already had a view and Claude disagreed, 60% switched sides. 77% of analysts repeated Claude's arguments, sometimes word for word. Only 15% credited the AI. Sources: Anthropic, Al Jazeera, Unite.AI.

item.title: AI agents just computer-checked the biggest proof in math history in 24 days
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The startup Axiom says its AI agents rewrote the Classification of Finite Simple Groups in Lean, a language computers can check line by line. About 100 mathematicians built the original over decades. Axiom's map of the proof. Dozens of agents wrote about 43.1 million lines of Lean code, with Axiom's mathematicians reviewing the hardest parts. On October 10, they proved the famous Monster group is simple. The agents flagged 34 notable departures from the published record, plus a gap in a key theorem from a 1986 paper. Sources: Axiom, RuntimeWire, TokenPost, Unite.AI.
